Petroleos de Venezuela SA Maintains Stable Export Volumes Amid Global Fluctuations

Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA) reported routine export volumes for May, reflecting continued stability in the country’s crude and refined product shipments despite shifting international market dynamics. According to figures released by the state-run oil producer and confirmed by the Venezuelan Hydrocarbons Trade Association, PDVSA exported an average of 650,000 barrels per day (bpd) last month, only a marginal increase from April’s 640,000 bpd.

“May’s numbers demonstrate our commitment to consistent supply for our international partners,” said Ignacio Rivas, a senior PDVSA official. “Our logistics and production teams have worked efficiently to meet contractual obligations.” The company’s key export destinations remained Asia and the Caribbean, with shipments consisting mainly of Merey and Boscan grades.

Local analysts note that the company’s ability to sustain steady output is significant given ongoing maintenance at several upgraders in the Orinoco Belt. “PDVSA’s export figures for May are in line with seasonal expectations,” commented Elena Márquez, an energy sector consultant with Caracas-based consultancy Grupo Enerxía. “There were no major fluctuations or disruptions observed in loading schedules.”

The Venezuelan Oil Workers Union confirmed routine operations and reported no significant labor issues in the period. “Our members continue to support operations at all major terminals,” said union spokesperson Pablo Figueroa.

PDVSA’s domestic refining throughput also remained stable, processing approximately 320,000 bpd, according to trade sources. The company expects similar performance in June, citing steady international demand and ongoing optimization of its export logistics.
